source_evidence.valid_bounded_use: Diagnosis of the represented linguistic functions.
limitations: The suite is not an estimate of deployment prevalence.

target_claim.statement: The functional-suite results justify automatically blocking English conversations under the same hate policy.
target_claim.attribution_note: Deliberately extended survey claim, not original authors’ wording.

S.reason: The hypothetical claim explicitly holds the hate policy fixed.

C.reason: Conversational history is outside the functional artifact tests.

O.reason: Session adjudication is not established by artifact-level functional cases.

P.reason: The constructed test distribution does not establish deployed conversation traffic performance.

E.reason: Threshold-specific blocking errors and consequences are not validated.

other_limitations: The suite is not an estimate of deployment prevalence.
The deliberately extended claim is the survey’s worked example, not a claim attributed to the HateCheck authors.

transport_test.benign_sensitive_controls: Benign-sensitive conversations under the same policy.

decision.unsupported_extension: The functional-suite results justify automatically blocking English conversations under the same hate policy.

title: Refusal detection to justified refusal

source_locations.section_title: Worked Claim Profiles and Transport Tests
source_locations.label: sec:worked-profiles

source_locations.description: Separate labels for harm and refusal.

provenance.verification_level: Checked against the supplied manuscript; primary studies not independently re-audited

source_evidence.original_endpoint: WildGuard’s separate prompt-harmfulness, response-harmfulness, and refusal-detection labels.
source_evidence.source_result: The source study distinguishes these tasks; refusal-detection F1 measures identification of a refusal.
source_evidence.valid_bounded_use: Identifying refusals and evaluating the separately defined task labels on the tested exchanges.
limitations: A refusal can still leak harmful information.
A safe response need not refuse.
This is an illustrative extended claim, not the WildGuard authors’ wording.

target_claim.statement: Refusal-detection F1 alone establishes justified blocking on the same exchanges.
target_claim.attribution_note: Deliberately extended survey claim, not original authors’ wording.

S.reason: Policy is fixed in the hypothetical extension.

C.reason: Input access and exchanges are fixed.

O.reason: A refusal-occurrence label does not establish refusal appropriateness.

E.reason: A blocking rule requires consequences and policy-grounded appropriateness, not refusal detection alone.

other_limitations: A refusal can still leak harmful information.
A safe response need not refuse.
This is an illustrative extended claim, not the WildGuard authors’ wording.

transport_test.design: Jointly assess the request’s policy status, response content, permitted safe alternatives, and intervention consequences. A new threshold on refusal occurrence is insufficient.
transport_test.retained_endpoint: WildGuard’s separate prompt-harmfulness, response-harmfulness, and refusal-detection labels.
transport_test.benign_sensitive_controls: Harmful requests and benign-sensitive requests, including safe non-refusal answers.
transport_test.acceptable_degradation: Must be prespecified; no numerical tolerance is supplied by this worked case.
transport_test.absolute_action_requirement: Must be established for the target action; no universal threshold is supplied.
transport_test.result: Proposed test only; no empirical bridge result reported.

decision.supported_claim: Refusal-detection performance supports the refusal-occurrence task under the tested conditions.
decision.unsupported_extension: Refusal-detection F1 alone establishes justified blocking on the same exchanges.
recommended_next_evidence: Jointly assess the request’s policy status, response content, permitted safe alternatives, and intervention consequences. A new threshold on refusal occurrence is insufficient.

title: One output to repeated-access exposure

source_locations.section_title: Worked Claim Profiles and Transport Tests
source_locations.label: sec:worked-profiles

provenance.verification_level: Checked against the supplied manuscript; primary studies not independently re-audited

source_evidence.original_endpoint: A hypothetical image-level failure rate under a fixed policy and interface.
source_evidence.source_result: For fixed independent trials at a given prompt and configuration, repeated-access risk is analytically 1 − (1 − r)^n; the worked claim uses n = 100.
source_evidence.valid_bounded_use: An image-level rate describes its stated single-output event. The analytic conversion applies only under the stated fixed-independent-trial assumptions.
limitations: The case is hypothetical and is not an empirical audit of a named paper.
The equation does not cover dependent or adaptive attempts without additional analysis.
Averaging prompt-specific rates before the nonlinear conversion need not equal averaging their repeated-access risks.

target_claim.statement: The same image-level failure rate estimates harm within 100 attempts, with policy and interface fixed and no enforcement action specified.
target_claim.attribution_note: Deliberately extended survey claim, not original authors’ wording.

S.reason: The hypothetical claim holds policy fixed.

O.target_condition: At least one harmful output within 100 attempts
O.reason: One-image failure and at least one failure within 100 attempts are different events.

P.target_condition: Repeated access with stated budget and stopping
P.reason: Repeated access changes the probability regime; correlated or adaptive attempts require a distinct analysis.

E.reason: No action is specified in this hypothetical claim. N does not mean demonstrated absence of evidence for a named action.

other_limitations: The case is hypothetical and is not an empirical audit of a named paper.
The equation does not cover dependent or adaptive attempts without additional analysis.
Averaging prompt-specific rates before the nonlinear conversion need not equal averaging their repeated-access risks.

transport_test.design: Measure prompt-level repeats with a declared stopping rule and quantify uncertainty at the prompt or session level; use the analytic conversion only for fixed independent trials.
transport_test.retained_endpoint: A hypothetical image-level failure rate under a fixed policy and interface.
transport_test.benign_sensitive_controls: Maintain a consistent policy and adjudication protocol across one-output and repeated-access measurements.
transport_test.acceptable_degradation: Must be prespecified; no numerical tolerance is supplied by this worked case.
transport_test.absolute_action_requirement: Not specified because this hypothetical target claim names no enforcement action.
transport_test.result: Proposed test only; no empirical bridge result reported.

decision.supported_claim: The source rate concerns its specified image-level event.
decision.unsupported_extension: The same image-level failure rate estimates harm within 100 attempts, with policy and interface fixed and no enforcement action specified.
recommended_next_evidence: Measure prompt-level repeats with a declared stopping rule and quantify uncertainty at the prompt or session level; use the analytic conversion only for fixed independent trials.

title: Static screening to component release

source_locations.section_title: Worked Claim Profiles and Transport Tests
source_locations.label: sec:worked-profiles

source_locations.description: Concept QuickLook sample, metric limitations, and author overlap.

provenance.verification_level: Checked against the supplied manuscript; primary studies not independently re-audited

source_evidence.original_endpoint: Concept QuickLook’s original NSFW categories in static single-file embedding inspection; no toxicity crosswalk is established by this case.
source_evidence.source_result: The manuscript describes SD 1.5/2.0 embedding inspection over 800 reviewed files (500 downloaded and 300 customized), with 15% marked NSFW. These numbers do not establish ecosystem prevalence.
source_evidence.valid_bounded_use: Configuration-bound static concept inspection can prioritize further investigation; it does not validate automatic release.
limitations: The reported Accuracy/FPR/FNR values are not jointly reconcilable under conventional binary definitions.
The metric inconsistency concerns evidence quality separately from coordinate support.
Several survey authors also authored Concept QuickLook.
The NSFW policy must not be silently relabeled targeted social harm or a general toxicity rate.

target_claim.statement: Single-file embedding inspection justifies automatic release across arbitrary compatible compositions while retaining the original NSFW categories.
target_claim.attribution_note: Deliberately extended survey claim, not original authors’ wording.
target_claim.action: Automatically release components across arbitrary compatible compositions.

S.reason: D retains the source NSFW endpoint; it does not establish a mapping to targeted social harm.

C.reason: Executed paths and arbitrary compatible compositions are not covered by a static single-file screen.

O.reason: Static similarity does not observe generated outcomes after loading.

P.source_condition: Named embedding settings and reviewed sample
P.target_condition: Composition distribution across bases, scales, triggers, and seeds
P.reason: The distribution of compositions, bases, triggers, scales, and seeds is untested by static similarity.

E.reason: Release costs and an operational release rule are not validated.

other_limitations: The reported Accuracy/FPR/FNR values are not jointly reconcilable under conventional binary definitions.
The metric inconsistency concerns evidence quality separately from coordinate support.
Several survey authors also authored Concept QuickLook.
The NSFW policy must not be silently relabeled targeted social harm or a general toxicity rate.

transport_test.design: Test both scanner-selected and scanner-cleared files on declared bases, scales, triggers, and seeds, with independent image adjudication and benign controls; reconcile the original metric definitions.
transport_test.retained_endpoint: Concept QuickLook’s original NSFW categories in static single-file embedding inspection; no toxicity crosswalk is established by this case.
transport_test.benign_sensitive_controls: Benign controls and behavioral audits of both scanner-selected and scanner-cleared components.
transport_test.acceptable_degradation: Must be prespecified; no numerical tolerance is supplied by this worked case.
transport_test.absolute_action_requirement: Must be established for the target action; no universal threshold is supplied.
transport_test.result: Proposed test only; no empirical bridge result reported.

decision.supported_claim: The static inspection feasibility result is bound to its original endpoint and tested configuration.
decision.unsupported_extension: Single-file embedding inspection justifies automatic release across arbitrary compatible compositions while retaining the original NSFW categories.
recommended_next_evidence: Test both scanner-selected and scanner-cleared files on declared bases, scales, triggers, and seeds, with independent image adjudication and benign controls; reconcile the original metric definitions.
